newsitem.title: CANADA: DBRS raises short-term Canada debt rating trend.
newsitem.headline: DBRS raises short-term Canada debt rating trend.

text.p: Dominion Bond Rating Service Ltd raised its credit rating trend on Canada's short-term obligations on Thursday to stable from negative, citing improvements in Canada's fiscal position and economic outlook.
DBRS also confirmed ratings of AAA for Canadian dollar long-term obligations, AA (high) for foreign-denominated long term obligations and R-1 for all short-term obligations.

The trend change reflects steady progress in the government's fiscal agenda, including a reduction in the deficit-GDP ratio and a projected end to new government financing requirements in 1998-99, DBRS said.

DBRS, however, said Canada's long-term rating trend remains negative since high levels of debt -- almost C$600 billion (US$440.2 billion) -- and significant net foreign indebtedness still haunt the fiscal outlook.
"A longer period of sustained progress is required to reduce significantly the potential effect of these exposures to the fiscal program," DBRS reported.
Canada's high levels of debt and foreign indebtedness continue to leave the government's fiscal track susceptible to a weakening U.S. economy or higher interest rates, the DBRS reported.

Renewed separatist activity in the French-speaking province of Quebec, though not a pressing issue at the moment, has the potential to induce large risk premiums into Canada's interest rates, DBRS added.
